app: Asterisk `queue_log` file monitoring via Universal Forwarder — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=voip sourcetype=asterisk:queue_log
| eval q=coalesce(queue, qname)
| eval is_abandon=if(event="ABANDON",1,0), is_enter=if(event="ENTERQUEUE",1,0), is_answer=if(event="CONNECT",1,0)
| bin _time span=1h
| stats sum(is_enter) as enters, sum(is_abandon) as abandons, sum(is_answer) as answers by _time, host, q
| eval abandon_rate=round(100*abandons/nullif(enters,0),2)
| eval sla_met=round(100*answers/nullif(enters,0),2)
| where enters>30 AND (abandon_rate>15 OR sla_met<75)
description: Surfaces 'Asterisk Queue Log Abandon Rate and Service Level Breach' patterns (UC-21.8.13) sourced from `index=voip` sourcetype `asterisk:queue_log`. Threshold bundle: `enters` > 30, `abandon_rate` > 15, or `sla_met` < 75; aggregation grain: `_time`, `host`, `q`; metrics: `enters`, `abandons`, `answers`. Watch terms: Asterisk, Queue, Log, Abandon, Rate.
value: Operations and risk leaders in Telecommunications use signals from Asterisk Queue Log Abandon Rate and Service Level Breach to move crews, budget, and customer or regulator communications while the situation is still controllable, so the organization steers from live telemetry rather than a post-incident report.
implementation: Monitor `/var/log/asterisk/queue_log` with correct line breaking (each line is one event). Extract `event`, `qname`/`queue`, and hold time fields if present on ABANDON. Tune thresholds: retail often tolerates higher abandons than emergency services. Join with workforce management schedules via lookup on `q`.
visualization: Line chart (abandon_rate, sla_met), Bar chart (worst queues), Heatmap (hour × queue).

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• `props.conf` `LINE_BREAKER` for queue_log pipe format.
• Clock sync between Asterisk and Splunk.

Step 1 — Validate event counts against `queue show stats`.

Step 2 — Exclude marketing test campaigns via ANI lookup.

Step 3 — Alert routing to WFM team with queue name.

Step 4 — Archive raw queue_log for regulatory retention if required.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Asterisk `queue_log` file monitoring via Universal Forwarder — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=asterisk:queue_log into voip. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, abandon_rate, enters, host`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
